name: Meinloh von Sevelingen
credit: Meinloh von Sevelingen, miniature in the Codex Manesse (Heidelberg, Cod. Pal. germ. 848), c. 1300–1340 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Meinloh von Sevelingen was an early minnesinger of the later twelfth century whose name points to a place in south-west Germany, usually identified with Söflingen near Ulm.
Two of his songs appear here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: Constant Love
poems.author: Meinloh von Sevelingen
poems.text:
I am fain of a lady; right well do I know wherefore.
Since I began to serve her, she still hath pleased me more and more.
Dearer and ever dearer even with every day is she,
Fairer and ever fairer, and well, in sooth, she pleaseth me.
She is rich in all honour, high of worth, and sweet and true.
If I died in her service
And came to life thereafter, once more that lady I should woo!

poems.title: The Message
poems.author: Meinloh von Sevelingen
poems.text:
I saw Summer's messengers, flowers as red as red could be.
Knowest thou, fair lady, what a knight hath offered thee?
His service all in secret Ne'er was his joy so great.
Now his heart is heavy, since he quitted thee of late.
Now make him glad and joyous e'er this summer-tide pass by!
Small will be his pleasure,
Till to his heart's contentment within thine arm at length he lie.
